metrics.outcome: Done: Identity confirmed every done-when item holds, with Audit's evidence. Open inputs for the Requester (not blocking): UPI ID and UPI QR code image; Bank account details for donations; Shelter phone number; Shelter WhatsApp number; Shelter email address; Shelter address and opening hours; Real pet profiles and photos; Real success stories and photos; Native Kannada speaker to review the Kannada text.
metrics.brief: A website for Paws Haven animal shelter in Mysuru: pets for adoption, donate, volunteer sign-up, success stories, and a Kannada version.

estimate_vs_charged.name: English single-page site with all sections

ceo_choices.note: options are shuffled before the CEO sees them; shown_first measures position bias, identity_first measures pull toward the option Identity listed first

open_inputs: UPI ID and UPI QR code image
Native Kannada speaker to review the Kannada text

review.verdict: The department met all 11 done-when items in one cycle with no redirects, refusals or rework, but this was a happy-path run that left negotiation, conflict, rework and holds untested.

identity.note: Charter and done verdict were clean and evidence-based [4][16]. It bundled three questions into one CEO ask [2] where the role file says one; the code did not flag it. Q2 and Q3 option 1 read as weak alternatives.

adaptation.note: Smallest useful split (English site, then Kannada), mapped to done-when, and it named the trade-off and the reserve risk itself [6]. It committed 47 of 50 up front, leaving no room for rework.

priority.note: Granted both at full estimate and said the 3 reserve is below one fix (8) [7], but did not COUNTER to protect a rework buffer. Its reason (every part maps to a done-when item) is goal relevance, which belongs to Adaptation and Identity. Only one turn, so bargaining is untested.

coordination.note: Stated its rule, respected the dependency and the file lock, no HOLD needed [9][11]. In [11] it added an acceptance checklist for the Builder, which edges into completion-check and Audit territory.

audit.note: Used the code check, filed findings per item, and used the right hand-off to Identity [15]. Gaps: no stated Kannada-mode overflow test, and no mention of the charter standards (alt text, contrast, no stored data). It passed 'opens a pre-filled message' items with only a warning.

ceo.note: Three decisions, each tied to user outcome, risk and reversibility, with trade-offs named [3]. It also ruled that open inputs do not block done, which Identity did not ask. Choices match the charter and caused no pauses.

builder.note: Executed both workflows as declared, 43.8 KB, no JS errors or overflow per [14]. Reports were short self-claims [10][12]; it did not flag that inquiry buttons cannot open a real chat until numbers exist.

went_well: All 11 done-when items passed with 0 failures, 0 redirects, 0 invalid moves, 0 validator or role refusals, 11 AI calls, 6.1 minutes.

The CEO resolved the three real value choices (UPI/bank only, pre-filled WhatsApp/email, full Kannada parity) at charter time [3], and they became rules the validator and Audit could check. No pauses were needed.
A code-run mechanical check (360px and 1280px overflow, JS errors, broken links) ran before Audit and gave it direct evidence [14].
Placeholders and sample entries were used instead of invented shelter facts, and the open inputs list is complete and clear [17].
problems: Thin test: 1 cycle, 1 proposal, 0 counters, 0 conflicts, 0 rework, 0 holds. The bargaining, Identity ruling, rework and hold paths were never exercised.

Possible miss on done-when items 3 and 5: Audit says the buttons 'only show the prepared message' until numbers are supplied [15], while the wording is 'opens a pre-filled WhatsApp or email message'. Passed as a warning with no click or link-format check. This is the main conversion path.
Mechanical check [14] does not say whether Kannada mode was tested at 360px, though the charter requires no overflow in Kannada and the CEO said Audit should test it [3]. Unverified.
Budget 47 of 50 with the reserve below one fix [6][7]. Any Audit failure would have needed a new proposal.
Estimate equals charged exactly (35/35, 12/12) with rate_card true, so the run cannot show whether Priority's or Adaptation's estimates were accurate.

The CEO position-bias metric disagrees with the chat. The log says identity_first 2 of 3 (original_pos 0,1,0), but the CEO's chat picks map to Identity's options 2, 3, 2 [2][3]. Also n=3, too small to read.
learnings: Keep: escalate the value choices to the CEO at charter time. Evidence: [3], pauses 0, no later policy disputes.

Change the test system: add a code check that clicks each inquiry and volunteer action and verifies a wa.me or mailto link with pre-filled text, and run the mechanical overflow check in Kannada mode too. Evidence: [14][15].
Reword done-when items 3 and 5 so they are testable as 'link is built with pre-filled text and a marked placeholder number', so Audit gives PASS or FAIL instead of a warning.

Test next: a tighter budget (for example 30) or a larger brief so Priority must COUNTER and bargain, and a run with a seeded defect so the Audit to Adaptation rework loop and the reserve rule are exercised. This run cannot say either works.
Test system: log actual model usage per workflow separately from the rate-card charge. Evidence: estimate equals charged on both workflows.
Test system: recheck how original_pos and shown_pos are logged against the options the CEO actually saw, and aggregate CEO choices over many runs before drawing any conclusion on bias.
Design: decide whether Identity may batch charter questions to the CEO. The role file says one, [2] sent three, and no code rule caught it. Enforce it or amend the file.
Design: Coordination had nothing to decide with two serial workflows (held_ever 0). Test it with independent workflows or a lock collision before judging its scheduling role.
